Self-hosting gives you your own services. It usually also gives you a second job.

Compose files, reverse proxies, disks filling at 2am, an update that breaks the stack while you’re away. Sparky does that job: it installs, wires up, updates, backs up and restarts what falls over, and asks you only when something needs a decision.

A real homelab, without the evenings it usually costs.

Install

Ask, don’t configure.

Name the thing you want. Sparky picks sane defaults, wires the storage and puts it behind a name that works on your network.

Maintain

Updates, backups, watching.

It updates itself and what it installed, backs up nightly and restarts dead services instead of failing quietly.

Own

Your hardware, your data.

Everything runs on the box in your house. No subscription owns your library, your files or your logs.

Extend

It grows with you.

Add a service later and it fits into what’s already there, sharing storage, network and backups.

The same open source, set up properly.

Nothing proprietary, nothing locked. If you outgrow Sparky, it is a Linux box with your data on it.
